archetype: Naya Dinosaur battlecruiser. Plan A is an eight-mana commander's combat-damage trigger; plan B is an enrage web that needs no combat step but does need a damage source of its own on the board. strategic_frame.json calls it a 'linear critical-mass ramp deck'; deck-audit matched no archetype keyword, so BASE targets applied and no aggro or combo override was used — read the ratio targets as starting points, per the audit's own first note.
verdict: The deck functions: it hits its turn-3 land drop 89.4% of the time, covers all five interaction classes, and carries 11 removal pieces inside an 18-card interactive suite — unusual for a linear typal list. What limits it is the top end. Six of the audit's 65 nonland entries sit at mana value 8+ — the commander among them — and goldfish puts Gishath's mean cast turn at 7.969 with 8.3% by turn 6, while exactly two maindeck cards can make him cheaper. The enrage web is not the ready fallback it looks like either: it is a conjunction of a converter body and a damage source, and no goldfish target measures the two together.

components.reading: Re-scoped from the deck's own 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' group, which the audit sizes at 6 and measures at 67.3%. Reading all six: Descendants' Path casts off the top of the library, Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual put a creature from HAND onto the battlefield, and Huatli's Roar chapter III searches a Dinosaur to hand. None of those four can touch a card in the command zone. Only Otepec Huntmaster ({1} less on Dinosaur spells) and Urza's Incubator ({2} less on the chosen type) make Gishath cheaper — a grep of every maindeck oracle text for cost reduction returns exactly four hits, and the other two, Blasphemous Act and Ghalta, Primal Hunger, reduce only themselves. The 67.3% is a real figure about a group that mostly does something else.

The declared connection kit: 5 cards, 62.2% assembled, 51.4% by turn 6. Two of the five are dead weight for the commander himself — Gishath already reads 'Vigilance, trample, haste', so Regisaur Alpha's 'Other Dinosaurs you control have haste' and Otepec Huntmaster's haste activation add nothing to his connection. The group also under-declares in the other direction: across all 89 maindeck entries only Rogue's Passage can make him unblockable and only Akroma's Will can grant him evasion at all (flying on one mode, protection from each colour on the other), and neither Akroma's Will nor Boros Charm nor Huatli's Roar chapter IV — the three double-strike grants — are group members.

The lowest measured rate of the six declared groups: 59.0% ever, 48.5% by turn 6. Read the five: Heroic Intervention's hexproof and Akroma's Will's protection from each colour do answer targeted exile and bounce, so the group is broader than 'indestructible' — but Eerie Interlude is the only member that dodges a non-targeted mass exile or bounce, and Flawless Maneuver the only one castable for nothing.

The declared group is seven and the simulation measures it at 73.7% assembled, 62.3% by turn 6. The 41.2% beside it in the audit is not a second measurement: it is `odds.opening_seven`, the closed-form hypergeometric for a 7-of, and it is the same calculation the redundancy citation's 41% comes from — the agreement is arithmetic, not corroboration. The label does not survive the same check. Reading all seven: only Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Forerunner of the Empire trigger on each Dinosaur entering. Garruk's Uprising triggers on any creature entering with power 4 or greater, which many but not all of the deck's Dinosaurs are — in stack 001's stipulated reveal three of the four entering Dinosaurs qualified and Ravenous Sailback did not. Curious Altisaur and Quartzwood Crasher both require combat damage to a player. Descendants' Path is an upkeep trigger that casts off the top of the library, and Regisaur Alpha is a static haste anthem plus a single ETB token; neither is a per-Dinosaur trigger at all. Three of the seven pay off a Dinosaur entering, which is the event Gishath's trigger actually produces.

Re-scoped from the deck's own 'Enrage engine drawn' group, which the audit sizes at 9 and measures at 82.4% assembled, 72.6% by turn 6. Reading all nine oracle texts, five convert damage into value: Ripjaw Raptor draws, Polyraptor copies itself, Ranging Raptors fetches a basic, Trapjaw Tyrant exiles a creature, and Wrathful Raptors redirects the damage at 'any target that isn't a Dinosaur'. The other four do something else — Bonehoard Dracosaur is an upkeep impulse engine, Temple Altisaur is a prevention shield ('prevent all but 1 of that damage'), Pugnacious Hammerskull's whole text is a stun-counter drawback on attack, and Trumpeting Carnosaur is a discover-5 ETB plus a one-shot discard ping. Temple Altisaur is still load-bearing for the web without being a converter: stack 004 (checker pass) uses its damage floor to make Blasphemous Act one-sided for the rest of the board, with the checker's own correction that Temple Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, eats the unprevented 13 and dies. Five cards is a 31.2% opening-seven class — the rate the audit reports for both of its own size-5 groups — so the 82.4% is a real figure about a nine-card set that is not all one function.

Not a declared group, and that is the finding: no target in goldfish_targets.json pairs an enrage body with a source of damage, so the conjunction the web actually needs has never been simulated. Six maindeck cards can damage your own Dinosaurs. Four are one-shots and Zacama's is repeatable only at {2}{R} a shot off a nine-mana body, leaving Forerunner of the Empire as the only free repeatable source. A six-card class is a 36.4% opening seven — the audit's figure for its own size-6 group — and a single named card is 7.1% by the redundancy citation. Every enrage line in this deck's stack folder that a checker has passed is ignited by Forerunner or by the bench's Marauding Raptor (002, 003, 005), or by Blasphemous Act (004) — which stack 004's scenario casts for {R} off nine creatures, so cost is not the objection to it: it is a one-shot, and it sweeps your own board with everyone else's unless Temple Altisaur is out to floor the 13 at 1 for your other Dinosaurs — Altisaur itself, and any non-Dinosaur you control, still take the full amount. Filed as `fodder` because it supplies what the `piece` converters consume; `ignition` names the commander-cost class above, and the two are disjoint.

gaps: There is no data/decks/gishath/deck_recon.json — the audit's freshness block reports recon absent. Nothing here is grounded in what strong Gishath lists actually run; the cost-reducer prescription is derived from this deck's own measured cast turn, not from inclusion rates. A recon pass would say whether the consensus fix is reducers, cheat-into-play effects, or simply more lands.
goldfish does not model cost reducers, rituals or extra card draw, and states so. Every commander-deployment figure in this document is therefore a conservative bound.

deck-audit matched no archetype from strategic_frame.json, so BASE ratio targets applied with no override. The frame calls the deck 'linear critical-mass ramp'; if it were re-tagged aggro, the creature and land targets would move and the ramp OVER reading would move with them.
bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so the floor of 4 is not staleness-checked against this list the way goldfish_metrics and mana_analysis are.
decklist.txt lists Wakening Sun's Avatar twice, once in the 99 and once on the bench. The audit counts the maindeck copy; the duplication is worth resolving before any swap touches that slot.

The card-advantage enumeration of fourteen sources is my reading of oracle text, not an audit figure. The audit's number is 6 and card_roles.json classifies 94.4% of this deck; Descendants' Path, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede, Rishkar's Expertise and Triumphant Chomp have no role entry at all.

All six of this deck's goldfish targets are authored as a single any_of group, so not one of them expresses a conjunction — which is why the enrage web's two halves have never been priced together. The schema allows it; the declaration does not use it.

findings.note: The document's central framing — that the enrage web 'needs a damage source the deck has to supply itself' — states a necessity the oracle text does not support. Every enrage trigger in the `piece` component reads 'Whenever this creature is dealt damage' with no source restriction (Ripjaw Raptor, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant, verified from cards.json), and Wrathful Raptors reads 'Whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage'. Combat damage from an opponent's attacker or blocker, and any damage-based removal pointed at your board, fire all five. The claim is right about PROACTIVE, on-your-terms ignition and wrong as stated about the web's requirements, and it is load-bearing in six places: verdict ('not the ready fallback it looks like ... a conjunction of a converter body and a damage source'), archetype ('does need a damage source of its own on the board'), components[5] (`fodder`, whose reading withdraws the measured 82.4% on the conjunction argument), single_points_of_failure[1] ('fodder — the free repeatable self-ping'), lean_into[0], and open_questions[4]. Note the goldfish assumption block ('Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal)') means no goldfish target could ever have measured opponent-sourced damage either way, so 'the conjunction the web actually needs has never been simulated' overstates what a re-declared target would settle. The enumerated facts underneath are all true and independently verified — six maindeck cards can damage your own Dinosaurs (Forerunner of the Empire, Zacama, Blasphemous Act, Itzquinth, Triumphant Chomp, Trumpeting Carnosaur; a regex over every maindeck oracle text returns no seventh, and Boros Charm and Wrathful Raptors are correctly excluded), four are one-shots, and Forerunner is the only free repeatable one. The defect is the modal leap from 'the only source you control' to 'the source the web needs'. The prescription survives: lean_into[0] already sizes the two adds off the commander's 7.969 cast turn, 'not off the enrage rate this entry withdraws'.
